decision_question: Which PIA owns competition show and travel workflow truth?
why_needed: The assessment domain crosses horse lifecycle scheduling and participant safeguarding but the portfolio permits no eleventh PIA
governing_context: Ten-item portfolio; Horse Lifecycle; Safeguarding; Relationship and Permission canons
options: A Item 08 primary with 04 and 06 contracts; B Item 04 primary; C Item 06 primary
benefits: A keeps participant and guardian risk with training operations while preserving horse and schedule owners
risks: A requires precise handoffs; B can overextend horse lifecycle; C can turn a scheduling engine into a domain owner
affected_actors: Riders; guardians; trainers; owners; staff; providers
affected_records_workflows: Entries; eligibility; horse assignment; travel plan; schedule; consent; incidents
privacy_implications: Minimize participant location and minor exposure; purpose-bound travel projections
security_implications: Do not infer eligibility or authority from schedule or entry status
safeguarding_implications: Guardian consent restrictions and safe-travel controls remain Item 08 invariants
offline_implications: Offline rosters and travel changes need versioned sync and visible freshness
financial_implications: Fees and refunds remain Item 09 contracts
evidence_audit_implications: Attributable eligibility consent change and incident evidence
implementation_implications: Requires cross-PIA interface requirements but no new PIA
recommended_answer: Select Option A: Item 08 owns competition/show/travel operations; Item 04 owns horse lifecycle and eligibility facts; Item 06 owns scheduling; Item 09 owns money
recommendation_rationale: Aligns workflow risk with participant safeguarding while preserving canonical owners
consequences_of_deferral: Affected normative scope remains provisional and Item 08 approval is blocked

decision_question: How are asset identity operational use and maintenance workflows allocated?
why_needed: Facility topology care execution and work coordination overlap
governing_context: Ten-item component map; Facility and Barn canons
options: A 02 identity 07 use 06 work orders; B all in 02; C all in 07
benefits: A preserves one source per concern and reusable work coordination
risks: A needs explicit versioned handoffs; B overextends Facility; C duplicates topology and scheduling
affected_actors: Facility operators; managers; staff; grooms; service providers
affected_records_workflows: Assets; fixtures; tack; equipment; inspections; maintenance requests; assignments; closures
privacy_implications: Location and security-sensitive asset details remain private by default
security_implications: Maintenance access never creates tenant or facility authority
safeguarding_implications: Hazards and safety-critical equipment require escalation and restricted visibility
offline_implications: Offline inspection and work-order queues need duplicate and conflict controls
financial_implications: Charges and vendor obligations remain Item 09
evidence_audit_implications: Asset lineage work-order changes completion and correction must be auditable
implementation_implications: Three interfaces; no new PIA or schema authority
recommended_answer: Select Option A: Item 02 owns asset/location identity; Item 07 owns care use and safety observations; Item 06 owns service-request scheduling and state
recommendation_rationale: Separates durable truth from operational use and generic work coordination
consequences_of_deferral: Items 02 06 and 07 cannot finalize overlapping scope

decision_question: Should reporting and analytics be a separate PIA or a cross-PIA contract surfaced by Item 05?
why_needed: A locked reporting canon exists but the portfolio prohibits an eleventh PIA without a new decision
governing_context: Ten-item portfolio; Reporting canon; Product Vision; Search; Privacy and Permission
options: A no new PIA: domain truth plus Item 05 shared surface; B create eleventh PIA; C assign all reporting to Item 05
benefits: A avoids duplicate truth; B centralizes but changes portfolio; C simplifies surface but risks shell-owned truth
risks: B changes the locked portfolio; C can create a competing source of truth; A requires disciplined cross-PIA metric contracts
affected_actors: All users; administrators; Founder; support; analysts
affected_records_workflows: Metrics; reports; projections; filters; exports; freshness and lineage
dependencies: All PIAs; Reporting Privacy Permission Audit and Records canons
privacy_implications: Purpose limitation aggregation suppression and export controls remain domain-aware
security_implications: Permission filtering and anti-enumeration apply to every projection
safeguarding_implications: Minor and safeguarding data cannot be exposed by aggregation
offline_implications: Offline analytics must show staleness and avoid unsupported completeness
evidence_audit_implications: Every metric requires definition owner source timestamp lineage and correction
implementation_implications: A requires shared interface contracts; no implementation authority
recommended_answer: Select Option A: do not create an eleventh PIA; each domain owns truth and metrics while Item 05 owns shared presentation and discovery
recommendation_rationale: Preserves portfolio control and prevents a reporting layer from becoming a competing system of record
consequences_of_deferral: Item 05 and cross-PIA reporting acceptance criteria remain provisional

decision_question: What review-runtime path should govern the next PIA review cycle?
why_needed: Current unrestricted approval-policy-never runtime fails repository role requirements
options: A provision compliant role sessions; B grant broad unrestricted exception; C defer all review
benefits: A preserves assurance boundaries; B is expedient but weakens custody and conflicts with default policy; C avoids invalid claims but stalls progress
risks: B increases tampering and assurance risk; C indefinitely blocks all substantive review
affected_actors: Founder; reviewers; evidence custodian; all downstream users
affected_records_workflows: Frozen review inputs permission records role outputs discrepancy reconciliation
dependencies: Qualified role configurations and frozen package
privacy_implications: Compliant lanes reduce unnecessary source exposure
security_implications: Read-only and bounded write isolation limit tampering and exfiltration
financial_implications: No direct money movement; review costs and delay only
evidence_audit_implications: PASS record before every role; immutable inputs; complete run evidence
implementation_implications: No application implementation; runtime setup only
recommended_answer: Select Option A: provision read-only/on-request/network-disabled reviewers and isolated bounded workspace-write/on-request/network-disabled writable roles; do not grant a broad exception
recommendation_rationale: This is the repository's fail-closed default and the only path that supports defensible independent-review claims
consequences_of_deferral: Every fresh-review completion and ready-for-Founder-review classification remains blocked
